_comment: Kontrakt makro dla hts-premarket. Sterowniki fundamentalne (nie-cenowe) zmapowane na kody assetow z universe.json. Kazdy sterownik ma ocene dowodu, wielkosc efektu z probka, warunek zlamania rezimu i zrodlo. NIE sa to sygnaly wejscia. Patrz MACRO.md.

meta.purpose: Graded, sourced macro drivers for the premarket macro header. Selection / sizing / hold context only.
meta.evidence_base: 57 primary full-text sources across 20 driver packets
meta.hard_rule: No driver in this file is an entry trigger. Entries belong to hts_logic.py. See MACRO.md section 2.

grade_scale.STRONG: academic + practitioner converge, clean magnitude, mechanism identified
grade_scale.PRACTITIONER: coherent mechanism + consensus, proof mixed or regime-dependent
grade_scale.WEAK: thin, contested, or holds only in a narrow regime
grade_scale.DECAYED: was real, faded in recent data - do not revive

status_scale.ALIVE: relationship holding in recent data as of research_asof
status_scale.BROKEN: relationship is currently failing - do NOT act on its sign
status_scale.CONDITIONAL: sign depends on a named regime state that must be read first

meta.layer_note: grade/magnitude/citations are CONTRACT (slow, curated, change only on new evidence). status is STATE (fast) - the shipped value is a research snapshot at research_asof; recompute it via state_check and write results to macro_state.json. Never edit status here from a computed reading.

FRED_CSV.note: Use the CSV endpoint. The JSON API at api.stlouisfed.org requires a key and returns 400 without one.

CFTC_SOCRATA.note: Keyless and filterable, e.g. ?commodity_name=GOLD. A free app token only removes throttling.

YAHOO_V8.note: Already used by data_yf.py. Unofficial and rate-limited; retry with backoff.

MANUAL.note: No free API exists. A human or an agent reads the release. Monthly or less frequent.

drivers.name: Central-bank policy surprise -> risk tide
drivers.mechanism: Markets reprice only the UNANTICIPATED component of a policy move; the anticipated part is already in the price. Transmission is mostly via the equity risk premium, not the risk-free rate.

inputs.series: FOMC / ECB / BoJ / BoE calendar + CME FedWatch implied path

drivers.sign: hawkish surprise -> risk down; dovish surprise -> risk up. Anticipated component -> no effect.

magnitude.detail: target factor -4.3% per 1pp; path/statement factor ~-1% per 1pp on equities but moves 5-10y yields 3-10x more
magnitude.sample: event-day regressions, R^2 0.12 daily to 0.35 intraday

drivers.regime_holds: always - the target/path lens is still the standard framework
drivers.regime_breaks: composition shifts: post-1994 the path/statement factor dominates because rate decisions themselves rarely surprise
drivers.decay: not decayed; core magnitude never overturned
drivers.state_check: Compare next scheduled meeting against CME FedWatch implied probability. A >20pp gap between market pricing and consensus = elevated surprise risk.
citations: Bernanke & Kuttner (2005), Journal of Finance 60(3)
Gurkaynak, Sack & Swanson (2005), International Journal of Central Banking 1(1)

drivers.name: Credit spreads (HY OAS / excess bond premium) -> equities
drivers.mechanism: Widening spreads signal deteriorating balance sheets and shrinking intermediary risk-bearing capacity - a credit-supply contraction that raises the cost of external finance ahead of cuts to investment and output. Stress appears in credit before equity admits it.
drivers.sign: widening -> equity headwind; compressing/falling -> corroborates risk-on continuation

magnitude.value: ~20bp excess-bond-premium shock -> ~7pp cumulative equity decline vs trend
magnitude.detail: 100bp GZ-spread rise -> >1.25pp GDP deceleration over 4 quarters; EBP shocks explain >10% of output variance
magnitude.sample: monthly bond-level, adj R^2 0.369 on 4Q-ahead GDP growth

drivers.regime_holds: post-mid-1980s, once a real below-investment-grade market existed. Robust across 1990-91, 2001, 2007-09.
drivers.regime_breaks: no known break. Traditional default-risk spreads (Baa-Aaa, CP-bill) lost forecasting power over the same period HY/GZ gained it.
drivers.decay: alive - the Fed publishes the EBP series monthly to present
drivers.state_check: 20-day change in BAMLH0A0HYM2. Widening >10% over 20d with equities flat or up = divergence worth flagging.
citations: Gilchrist & Zakrajsek (2012), American Economic Review 102(4)
Gertler & Lown (2000), NBER WP 7549 / Oxford Review of Economic Policy 15(3)

drivers.name: USD/JPY -> Nikkei (weak-yen exporter lift)
drivers.mechanism: Japan's largest listed firms are major exporters. Yen depreciation raises the yen value of USD revenue and improves competitiveness, lifting an export-dominated index.

magnitude.value: 1% yen depreciation -> +0.63% to +1.12% on the aggregate index
magnitude.detail: exposure 0.631 (2001-2012) roughly doubled to 1.117 (2013-2018) post-Abenomics; firm-level residual ~0.52
magnitude.sample: aggregate market exposure regressions; 227 exporters at firm level

drivers.regime_holds: across two periods and two methods; strengthening rather than fading
drivers.regime_breaks: BoJ's 2024 exit from negative rates and YCC is an emerging regime-change risk - flagged, not confirmed
drivers.decay: alive through 2018 sample end; strongest FX-to-index link on this board
drivers.state_check: 20-day change in USD/JPY. Confirm the Nikkei lean agrees with the yen direction; a disagreement is worth flagging, not overriding.
citations: Thorbecke (2022), RIETI DP 22-E-003 / Japan and the World Economy
Ito, Koibuchi, Sato & Shimizu (2016), NBER WP 21040

drivers.name: Silver = leveraged asymmetric gold + industrial demand
drivers.mechanism: Silver tracks gold's monetary and safe-haven demand with amplified, asymmetric moves, while carrying an industrial-cyclical component gold lacks - now the majority of its demand.

inputs.series: Silver Institute World Silver Survey (industrial demand)

drivers.sign: same direction as gold, amplified; plus an independent industrial-cycle component

magnitude.detail: shock asymmetry gold->silver ~1.25% vs silver->gold ~0.07%; industrial demand 59% of consumption (2024), up from ~51% a decade earlier; solar PV 11% -> 29% of industrial demand

drivers.regime_holds: silver lags gold on the initial risk-off leg (haven flows favour gold first), catches up or overshoots in reflation legs
drivers.regime_breaks: industrial tilt adds cyclical sensitivity gold lacks - in a growth scare silver can fall while gold rises
drivers.decay: not decayed - strengthening; industrial share rising
drivers.state_check: Read gold's own driver state first (D2+D11), then apply beta. Check whether the current leg is monetary (silver follows) or cyclical (silver diverges).
citations: Burnette & De Pessemier (2026), World Gold Council
Silver Institute, World Silver Survey 2025
Vigne, Lucey, O'Connor & Yarovaya (2017), International Review of Financial Analysis 52

drivers.name: Central-bank gold buying + physical/ETF flows -> gold
drivers.mechanism: Central banks buy gold for reserve diversification and sanctions insurance - gold can be vaulted outside the sanctioning system, unlike FX reserves that can be frozen. This buying is largely price-insensitive, so it persists even as real yields rise. It is the documented override of D2.

inputs.series: World Gold Council Gold Demand Trends (tonnage)

drivers.sign: sustained >1000t/yr official-sector buying -> structural bid under gold that can override the real-yield link

magnitude.detail: gold's share of aggregate international reserves rose 9% (2008) to 16% (2024); sanctions raise a country's gold-reserve share ~2pp and volume ~130t
magnitude.sample: country panel 2012-2023; 14 EM active diversifiers identified 1999-2021

drivers.regime_holds: post-2022, intensifying - the three highest official-buying years on record are consecutive
drivers.regime_breaks: unknown - both primary sources frame it as a structural post-GFC shift, not a one-off shock
drivers.state_check: Latest WGC quarterly tonnage vs the ~500t/yr pre-2022 baseline. Above it, treat D2's sign as suspended.
citations: Arslanalp, Eichengreen & Simpson-Bell (2023), IMF WP/23/14
Weiss (2025), Fed IFDP No. 1420
drivers.warning: The circulating claim that CB buying explains 10-15% of the 2022-24 move could NOT be traced to a primary source. It is a practitioner estimate, not a finding. Do not render it as a number.

drivers.name: Real yields (10Y TIPS) -> gold (opportunity cost)
drivers.mechanism: Gold pays no coupon, so the real 10Y yield is its opportunity cost. Rising real yields make bonds and cash relatively more attractive and push gold down.
drivers.sign: real yields up -> gold down (INVERTED - and currently not holding, see status)

magnitude.value: 1pp rise in real 10Y -> -13.1% real gold price (annual levels)
magnitude.detail: -3.4% per 1pp on quarterly innovations; daily TIPS coefficient -0.011; correlation of real yield vs real gold price -0.82 (US monthly 1997-2012), falling to -0.31 on a longer UK robustness sample
magnitude.sample: three independent specifications, all negative and significant

drivers.regime_holds: cleanly ~2001-2021. The negative co-movement does not appear before 2001.
drivers.regime_breaks: BROKE 2022-2024. The ~-0.73 rolling 12-month correlation collapsed to ~+0.03 as gold rose WITH rising real yields, overridden by D11.
drivers.decay: structurally intact and expected to reassert once the override fades, but a multi-year override is exactly what a position-holder feels
drivers.state_check: MANDATORY PAIRING. Compute the rolling 12-month correlation between DFII10 and gold. If it is not solidly negative, D2 is suspended and D11 governs. Never emit a gold lean from D2 alone.
citations: Erb & Harvey (2013), NBER WP 18706 / Financial Analysts Journal 69(4)
Barsky, Epstein, Lafont-Mueller & Yoo (2021), Chicago Fed Letter No. 464
drivers.warning: This is the single driver an LLM is most likely to get wrong from pretraining. The textbook relationship has been failing for three years. Never hard-code the pre-2022 sign.

drivers.name: VIX term structure -> volatility carry (NOT a VIX forecast)
drivers.mechanism: The slope between spot VIX and 3-month VIX reflects a variance risk premium - compensation for tail risk - not the expected path of spot VIX. Contango predicts positive carry for short-vol positions; it does not predict that VIX will fall.
drivers.sign: contango (VIX < VIX3M) -> short-vol carry positive; deep backwardation -> carry flips

magnitude.value: -1.70% to -0.72% per day across maturities (variance swaps)
magnitude.detail: 1pp of basis -> ~79bp next-month futures move; a hedged short-contango / long-backwardation strategy ~20%/yr at 5x margin, robust to costs and to excluding 2008-09
magnitude.sample: 33 of 36 regressions significant across 18 vol assets

drivers.regime_holds: broadly; magnitude survives excluding the 2008-09 crisis
drivers.regime_breaks: flips in the deepest-backwardation quintile - extreme stress
drivers.decay: confirmed through 2013; no post-2013 test located. Structural risk premium, not an obvious arbitrage.
citations: Johnson (2017), Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 52(6)
Simon & Campasano (2014), Journal of Derivatives 21(3)
drivers.warning: Contango does NOT mean 'VIX will fall'. That specific claim is explicitly unsupported by both primary sources.

drivers.name: US dollar -> gold (denominator) and global risk
drivers.mechanism: Gold is quoted and mostly traded in USD, so broad dollar depreciation mechanically lifts the USD gold price. Dollar weakness also coincides with looser global financial conditions.

inputs.role: DXY spot - already in universe.json as asset DXY

magnitude.detail: all coefficients significant (JPY -0.14 t=-5.46; CHF -0.24 t=-8.85) but R^2 only 6-15%. The authors' own verdict: 'little connection between currency returns and gold returns.'

drivers.regime_holds: sign consistently negative across the whole 1975-2022 window
drivers.regime_breaks: never clean - low R^2 is stable, not a recent fade. Gold rose in nearly every currency simultaneously 1975-2022.
drivers.decay: not decayed - the linkage is definitional
citations: Erb & Harvey (2013), NBER WP 18706
Arslanalp, Eichengreen & Simpson-Bell (2023), IMF WP/23/14
drivers.warning: R^2 below 15% means this is a directional check only. Too noisy to size on alone.

drivers.name: Risk regime - gold/equity correlation sign, VIX as state
drivers.mechanism: Gold is a hedge (near-zero or negative correlation with equities on average) but a true safe haven - sharply negative co-movement - ONLY in the extreme left tail of equity returns. VIX is overwhelmingly a contemporaneous mirror of the current move, not a forecast of the next one.
drivers.sign: in the equity tail only: gold up while equities down. Outside the tail: correlation near zero or positive.

magnitude.value: tail effect at the 1% quantile: US -0.018, UK -0.296, Germany -0.073
magnitude.detail: bull-to-bear correlation shift of 0.1-0.3; the safe-haven bid is gone within ~15 trading days of a shock

drivers.regime_breaks: bull and calm regimes - correlation is near-zero or positive. UK stayed at +0.13 to +0.15 across the whole sample.
drivers.decay: not decayed, but short-lived by nature - ~15 trading days
drivers.state_check: Rolling 60-day correlation of GC=F vs ^GSPC returns, plus the VIX level. Only a solidly negative correlation AND an elevated VIX puts you in the safe-haven window.
citations: Baur & Lucey (2010), Financial Review 45
Coudert & Raymond-Feingold (2011), Economics Bulletin 31(2)
Hibbert, Daigler & Dupoyet (2008), Journal of Banking & Finance 32
drivers.warning: A STANDING 'gold up therefore short equities' rule is wrong most of the year. The opposition is real only in the tail and it decays inside three weeks. Also: VIX same-day R^2 is 42-78% vs an order of magnitude weaker one day later - it describes, it does not predict.

drivers.name: 10Y nominal yield -> growth/tech equity (duration lever)
drivers.mechanism: Growth and tech value sits mostly in distant cash flows. Discounting those at a higher 10Y shrinks their present value disproportionately versus value and cyclicals. Formally, bond duration applied to equities.

inputs.role: already in universe.json as asset US10

drivers.sign: 10Y up -> growth/tech headwind (INVERTED), strongest on NQ

magnitude.value: Nasdaq -35% vs S&P-ex-tech -20% over Jan to mid-Oct 2022
magnitude.detail: structurally, high-duration stocks earn 1.10%/month less than short-duration cross-sectionally; equity duration correlates -0.67/-0.79 with book-to-market

drivers.regime_breaks: size scales with how sharp the rate move is and how priced-for-perfection the growth premium is. 2022 was uniquely sharp.
drivers.decay: not decayed - 2022 is the strongest confirmation on record; the duration math is definitional
drivers.state_check: 20-day change in DGS10. Use it to weight NQ against YM/ES, not to call direction alone.
citations: Dechow, Sloan & Soliman (2004), Review of Accounting Studies 9
Weber (2018), Journal of Financial Economics 128(3)
Kim, Nissim & Song (2024), Columbia Business School WP

drivers.name: Inflation surprise (CPI/PCE) -> US 10Y yield
drivers.mechanism: Nominal 10Y = real yield + breakeven inflation compensation. CPI surprises move the long end by updating expected inflation and, secondarily, the risk premium. The SIZE of that pass-through depends entirely on whether inflation is currently salient.
drivers.sign: upside CPI surprise -> yields up -> growth-equity and gold headwind. Magnitude is regime-dependent, not a fixed beta.

magnitude.value: ~0.6bp per 1-SD CPI surprise in 2009-2020 vs ~4.5bp in 2021-2023 - a ~7x jump
magnitude.detail: two-thirds of the rise came from expected-rate and inflation-expectation updating, one-third from risk premia. Unmatched by any of the other 15 releases tested.

drivers.regime_holds: when inflation is salient and attention is on it
drivers.regime_breaks: negligible and statistically insignificant when inflation is quiescent
drivers.decay: the Fisher mechanism is permanent; the pass-through MAGNITUDE decays toward zero whenever inflation stops being front-of-mind
drivers.state_check: Read the current inflation regime before weighting a CPI day. High and volatile T10YIE = salient regime = weight CPI day risk up sharply.
citations: Fleming & Remolona (1997), FRBNY Economic Policy Review 3(4)
Gurkaynak, Sack & Wright (2008), FEDS / AEJ:Macro
Kroner (2025), FEDS 2025-022

drivers.name: EUR/USD -> DAX and the European export indices
drivers.mechanism: DAX firms are heavily export-weighted (~77% of DAX revenue earned abroad). A weaker euro raises the home-currency value of USD-denominated export revenue. The same export channel extends to CAC, Euro Stoxx and IBEX, which is why they are listed as inherited targets.

magnitude.value: 10% DM depreciation vs USD -> +1.4% to +1.7% average DAX-constituent return
magnitude.detail: common exposure 0.139-0.172, significant; export-share coefficient 6.84 - 1pp more export share adds 0.07 to exposure

drivers.regime_breaks: FLIPS. DAX-dollar exposure went NEGATIVE 1980-85 during the strong-dollar recession (-0.308) before returning to +0.447 by 1991-95. DAX-GBP/EUR exposure weakened after Brexit.
drivers.decay: mechanism alive as of 2022 revenue data; the last clean econometric coefficient is from 1995. No modern EUR/USD-DAX regression located.
drivers.state_check: 20-day change in EUR/USD. Treat as a same-direction supporting factor only.
citations: Entorf & Jamin (2003/2007), German Economic Review 8(3)
Andrikopoulos, Dassiou & Zheng (2020), International Review of Financial Analysis 68
drivers.warning: F40, FESX and ES35 are INHERITED from the shared export mechanism, not independently measured. Grade them one step below DAX.

drivers.name: GBP/USD -> FTSE 100 (overseas earners)
drivers.mechanism: About 75-80% of FTSE 100 revenue is earned outside the UK. A weaker pound raises the sterling-translated value of that foreign revenue.
drivers.sign: pound weaker -> FTSE tailwind (INVERTED) - but the realised sign is unstable, see regime_breaks

magnitude.value: no stable statistical beta - the sign itself flips
magnitude.detail: overseas revenue share ~75-80%, confirmed by two sources nine years apart. But market-level FX exposure flipped from significantly POSITIVE pre-Brexit (2014-16) to significantly NEGATIVE post-Brexit (2016-18), net insignificant full-sample.

drivers.regime_breaks: demonstrated sign flip around Brexit. The study used GBP/EUR, not GBP/USD; UK-US rate differentials are a possible confound.
drivers.decay: revenue-share mechanism alive through 2022; statistical evidence only to 2018
drivers.state_check: Do not emit a FTSE lean from GBP alone. Require agreement with D4 or D9 first.
citations: Andrikopoulos, Dassiou & Zheng (2020), International Review of Financial Analysis 68
Capital Group (2013) and FTSE-Russell/LSEG (2022) revenue-share data
drivers.warning: Weakest of the three FX-to-index links. Only 1 primary source plus 2 data sources - below the 2-primary bar used everywhere else in this contract. Flagged, not hidden.

drivers.name: US day session -> European overnight gap (spillover)
drivers.mechanism: US markets close hours before Europe opens. Overnight order flow, futures and not-yet-priced information carry over, producing a directional US-to-Europe lead-lag, not the reverse.
drivers.sign: prior US session direction -> same-direction European early-session bias

magnitude.detail: ~0% in US expansions, 6.8% in US recessions - the tradable component is recession-concentrated and fragile. The structural linkage is stronger: aligning DAX one day after the Dow produces one dominant shared eigenvalue, with the reverse-direction placebo showing nothing.
magnitude.sample: 60 DAX and Dow constituents (structural); monthly predictive regressions

drivers.regime_holds: contemporaneous linkage is structural and strengthening; the tradable drift concentrates in recessions
drivers.regime_breaks: the monthly predictive component is ~0% in expansions
drivers.decay: all sources dated - structural evidence ends 1999, predictive ends 2010. Today's overnight-futures-dominated structure may transmit differently. Flagged as unconfirmed post-2010.
drivers.state_check: Prior ^GSPC session return. Relevant for the 06:30 UTC pre-EU run only, not the 13:00 run.
citations: Drozdz, Grummer, Ruf & Speth (2001), Physica A 294
Siliverstovs / Rapach, Strauss & Zhou - US role in international predictability
drivers.warning: Do NOT measure this off the raw DAX opening quote. The opening auction is illiquid and the literature explicitly warns that using it produces spurious results.

drivers.name: Platinum - auto/industrial demand and South African supply
drivers.mechanism: Platinum's price is set by industrial and autocatalyst demand against a concentrated, fragile South African supply chain (grid instability, strikes) - not by monetary or safe-haven flows. Its gold correlation is real but historically unstable, even sign-flipping over multi-year windows.

inputs.series: World Platinum Investment Council Platinum Quarterly

drivers.sign: supply disruption -> up; auto/industrial demand weakness -> down. Gold linkage is secondary and unreliable.

magnitude.value: South Africa >70% of global primary output; autocatalyst ~38-39% of demand
magnitude.detail: fourth consecutive annual structural deficit (-297 koz for 2026); above-ground stocks below 3 months' cover. Two independent official bodies agree on both figures.

drivers.regime_holds: supply shocks are idiosyncratic and untied to gold's macro drivers
drivers.regime_breaks: price correlation with gold flips sign across multi-year windows; cointegration strength tracks the business cycle, not crisis regimes
drivers.decay: supply/demand not decayed and live through 2026. Academic pricing studies are all 2006-2017 vintage with no update located.
drivers.state_check: Latest WPIC quarterly balance plus any live SA supply headline.
citations: SFA (Oxford), The Platinum Market and Platinum Price Drivers
World Platinum Investment Council, Platinum Quarterly Q1 2026
drivers.warning: Never treat PL as a gold proxy. It is a distinct industrial-cyclical bet. Weakest-evidenced of the metals - industry-data-led, and the academic pricing evidence was reachable only secondhand.

drivers.name: COT positioning extremes - ALIVE on softs/energy/FX, DEAD on metals and indices
drivers.mechanism: Hedging-pressure theory: hedgers pay speculators a risk premium to absorb non-marketable risk, so speculator positioning should predict returns. This REQUIRES a genuine, economically-motivated hedging population - present in physical commodities (farmers, refiners) and FX, but diluted in financial futures and precious metals where 'commercial' classification is murky and macro flows dominate.
drivers.sign: commercial/speculator positioning at a >80 or <20 percentile extreme -> mean-reversion pressure. Mid-range is noise everywhere.

magnitude.value: large-spec strategy: 2.38%/month in corn (t=1.98), 2.88%/month in yen (t=2.75) vs 0.19%/month in S&P 500 (t=0.13, insignificant)
magnitude.detail: same method, opposite outcome by asset class. On precious metals: of ~30 extreme-signal tests across gold/silver/platinum, only 2 reject the null - chance level. Granger p-values 0.28-0.86.
magnitude.sample: 15 US futures markets; separately, weekly percentile extremes on precious metals

drivers.regime_holds: agriculture, energy and FX - markets with real physical hedgers
drivers.regime_breaks: financial futures and precious metals - statistically insignificant
drivers.decay: not decayed-from-strong. Structurally weak on financials across both samples, i.e. alive-as-weak for 20+ years.
drivers.state_check: Weekly percentile rank of net positioning over a 3-year lookback. Only >80 or <20 carries any signal, and only on the four permitted targets.
citations: Wang (2003), Journal of Futures Markets 23(1)
Zhang & Laws (2013), University of Liverpool WP
drivers.warning: This is the driver most likely to be wrongly generalised. The internet treats COT as a universal indicator. It is statistically dead on gold, silver, platinum and every equity index in this universe. targets_excluded is a hard list, not a suggestion.

drivers.name: ISM / PMI growth cycle -> equities (SIGN FLIPS BY CYCLE STAGE)
drivers.mechanism: Real-activity news always lifts expected cash flows, but its discount-rate effect depends on cycle position. In a slack economy good growth news barely moves rates so stocks rise. In a hot economy the same news raises inflation and hike expectations, the discount effect dominates, and stocks FALL on 'good' data.

inputs.series: ISM Manufacturing and Services PMI (ismworld.org, or DBnomics ISM/pmi)

drivers.sign: REGIME-DEPENDENT - no fixed sign. Must read cycle stage first.

magnitude.value: -0.84% S&P daily return per 1pp unanticipated activity rise in a HOT state (significant) vs +0.12% in a SLACK state (insignificant)
magnitude.detail: the unconditional average effect is ~zero, which is why naive PMI-return correlations look like noise. ISM surprise coefficients on S&P futures jump-variance are insignificant (p>0.1) - weaker than payrolls or retail sales - while the same surprises DO significantly move Treasury futures.
magnitude.sample: S&P 500 daily; separately S&P and 30Y bond futures

drivers.regime_holds: the regime mechanism itself is confirmed across both samples
drivers.regime_breaks: the sign flips by cycle stage - this IS the finding
drivers.decay: ISM-to-equities was already weak throughout 1994-2014, not faded-from-strong
drivers.state_check: Direction over the LAST THREE PRINTS, never one. And you must classify cycle stage (slack vs hot) before assigning a sign.
citations: McQueen & Roley (1993), Review of Financial Studies 6(3)
Huang (2015), Fed FEDS 2015-097
drivers.warning: The widely circulated '4.5x edge' figure for ISM direction traces to NO primary source found in a full search. Do not render it. Included here at WEAK grade only because the regime mechanism is worth knowing; it is not a filter.

drivers.name: Yield curve (2s10s, 10Y-3M) -> recession/cycle
drivers.mechanism: Tightening raises short rates faster than long rates, flattening or inverting the curve while real activity slows. Separately, investors pricing future cuts pull long yields down directly.
drivers.sign: inversion -> multi-quarter risk-off cycle bias (CURRENTLY FAILING - see status)

magnitude.value: out-of-sample recession-probability pseudo-R^2 peaks at 0.328 three quarters ahead
magnitude.detail: +1.30 GNP-growth per 1pp of spread; recession probability exceeded 30% before all 6 recessions since 1968 with zero false signals on a monthly-average basis through 2006

drivers.regime_holds: clean 1968-2001, six for six, no false positives
drivers.regime_breaks: BROKEN SINCE 2022. The deepest and longest inversion since the early 1980s (~Oct-2022 to Dec-2024) with no recession dated through mid-2026 - the longest false-positive stretch on record.
drivers.decay: not yet 'decayed' but no longer a spotless record. A filter mid-failure is not a filter.
drivers.state_check: Report the curve as CONTEXT ONLY while status is BROKEN. Do not let it vote until a recession either confirms or the inversion resolves cleanly.
citations: Estrella & Hardouvelis (1991), Journal of Finance 46(2)
Estrella & Mishkin (1998), Review of Economics and Statistics 80(1)
Estrella & Trubin (2006), NY Fed Current Issues 12(5)
drivers.warning: STRONG grade, BROKEN status - and that combination is the point. High historical pedigree does not license current use.

ES.note: Barely a leaf - the S&P IS the broad risk barometer. It is driven by the global tier rather than by a private driver.

NQ.note: Most rate-sensitive index on the board. D6 is its distinguishing driver.

YM.note: Cyclical/value tilt, least rate-sensitive US index.

F40.note: Export channel inherited from DAX (D14). Not independently measured - grade one step below DAX.

ES35.note: IBEX appears in the Brexit FX-exposure study alongside FTSE and DAX, but no dedicated packet exists.

FTSE.note: D16 is the weakest FX link in the contract. Heavy energy and miner weighting also ties FTSE to commodity prices - mechanism acknowledged, not researched.

NIKKEI.note: D15 is the strongest FX-to-index link on the whole board.

HS.note: Hang Seng has no dedicated research packet. China policy, property credit and mainland flows are the obvious drivers and none of them are in the evidence base. Named stub, not a silent gap.

VX.note: VIX is a STATE gauge, not a forecast. See D3 and D18 warnings.

GC.note: MANDATORY PAIRING: D2 and D11 must be read together. D2 alone is currently misleading.

SI.note: Read gold's state first, then apply beta ~1.3. Industrial cycle is an independent second leg.

HG.note: Copper has no dedicated packet. It is the classic global-growth and China-construction proxy; D13 and D1 are inherited approximations, not measured. Named stub.

PA.note: Palladium has no packet. Same autocatalyst family as platinum (D20) but with different supply geography (Russia-weighted). Do not silently apply D20.

WBS.note: COT is ALIVE here - energy has real physical hedgers. OPEC policy, inventories and supply geopolitics are the primary drivers and are not in the evidence base.

CC.note: COT is ALIVE on softs. Weather and West African supply are the primary drivers and are not researched.

KC.note: As CC - Brazilian weather and supply.

DXY.note: DXY is an INPUT to other assets (D1), not a target. Do not emit a macro lean for DXY itself from this contract.

US10.note: Primarily an INPUT (D6, D7 feed off it). D7 is the one driver pointing AT it.

GBPJPY.note: COT is ALIVE on FX. Rate differentials and carry are the primary drivers and are not researched.

BTC.note: No crypto research exists in the evidence base. D9 is a generic risk-tide inheritance only. Everything crypto-specific - ETF flows, halving, on-chain - is absent. Named stub.

rejected.name: M2 / global liquidity / net liquidity (WALCL - TGA - RRP)
rejected.reason: In a G5 global VAR the asset-price response to an excess-liquidity shock is 'tiny and not statistically significant' globally, and an insignificant FALL for the US. The Fed-balance-sheet signal has R^2 of only 1-10% at 1-24 month horizons. The popular WALCL-TGA-RRP formula has NO peer-reviewed test of any kind - it is a chart construct. It fit only 2020-22, one unprecedented QE-plus-fiscal shock, then decoupled as QT and RRP drainage broke the arithmetic.
citations: Ruffer & Stracca (2006), ECB WP 696
Ruman (2022), Journal of Economic Studies 49(2)

rejected.name: COT on metals and equity indices
rejected.reason: Statistically insignificant specifically on gold, silver, platinum and financial futures. See D12 targets_excluded. This is a CONFIRM, not an untested prior - two independent samples spanning 1992-2012.
citations: Wang (2003), Journal of Futures Markets 23(1)
Zhang & Laws (2013), University of Liverpool WP

rejected.name: VIX as a directional forecast
rejected.reason: VIX moves are almost entirely contemporaneous: same-day return t-statistic on the VIX change is 110-208, dropping to 7-31 at the first lag. Same-day R^2 is 42-78% versus an order of magnitude weaker one day later. It is a mirror of the move that already happened. Keep it as a STATE gauge (D3) and as a term-structure carry input (D18) - never as a direction call.
citations: Hibbert, Daigler & Dupoyet (2008), Journal of Banking & Finance 32

rejected.name: Gold/silver ratio as a mean-reversion timer
rejected.reason: Linear cointegration is REJECTED (CUSUM 2.301 at 1%); a Johansen trace of 9.65 against a 15.19 critical value fails to reject NO cointegration. The classical monetary-twins relationship has been decaying since ~1990 across three independent studies. Only a crisis-conditional comovement survives. An 'extreme' ratio reading carries no reliable reversion timetable.
citations: Escribano & Granger (1998), Journal of Forecasting 17(2)
Ciner (2001), Global Finance Journal 12
Schweikert (2017), Resources Policy

rejected.name: A standing gold-versus-equities inverse rule
rejected.verdict: WRONG MOST OF THE YEAR - do not build
rejected.reason: The gold-equity opposition is real ONLY in the extreme left tail of equity returns (1-2.5% quantile) or in bear markets, and it decays within ~15 trading days. In bull and calm regimes the correlation is near zero or positive. A standing rule would be wrong most of the time. See D3.
citations: Baur & Lucey (2010), Financial Review 45
Coudert & Raymond-Feingold (2011), Economics Bulletin 31(2)

rejected.name: Calendar and seasonality edges
rejected.reason: Tested and dead in recent data: the pre-FOMC 24-hour drift died after 2016; the 8-9 CET overnight-drift hour died after 2021 by its own authors' update; the DAX has ZERO persistent calendar anomalies out of 188 tested; gold weekday folklore is dead in futures. Seasonality at '>65% of 10 years consistent' is coin-flip territory multiplied across 252 calendar days - guaranteed false positives.
citations: Multiple - see the time-edges research lane

rejected.name: A weighted composite score (e.g. COT 35% / macro 30% / valuation 20% / seasonal 15%)
rejected.reason: Those weights are one author's prior. No data derives them. A weighted average of individually unproven signals looks scientific and is not. Each driver must be readable and testable ALONE. If a composite is ever wanted, it has to be earned from measured outcomes, not asserted at design time.
citations: Assumption audit of the source blueprint

rejected.name: CONFLICT = NO TRADE (a hard veto when macro disagrees with the chart)
rejected.reason: A hard veto from an unproven composite would have blocked real winners. This overlay has zero proven track record on this system's own results. Record CONFLICT as a logged flag; never let it block. Only measured outcomes may ever promote it to a rule.
